functional_description: This feature represents the core cytotoxic machinery programme of mature NK cells, characterized by expression of granule-associated cytolytic proteins and signaling adaptors. The signature reflects activated NK cells with robust killing capacity, predominantly enriched in CD56high bone marrow resident NK cells that execute cytotoxic functions through granule exocytosis.
key_evidence: GNLY: Granulysin is a hallmark cytotoxic granule protein with antimicrobial activity, directly marking cytolytic NK cells
PRF1: Perforin forms membrane pores essential for granzyme delivery and target cell lysis, core cytotoxicity machinery
NKG7: Natural killer granule protein 7 is an integral granule membrane component specifically marking NK cytotoxic capacity
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor enabling KIR and activating receptor signaling required for cytotoxic NK activation
CTSW & CST7: Cathepsin W and cystatin F represent granule serine/cysteine proteases regulating cytolytic activity
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry co-staining of CD56 subsets with perforin, granulysin, and CD94/NKG2A to confirm enrichment in mature cytotoxic NK populations, particularly CD56dim peripheral NK cells.

functional_description: This feature represents mature, highly cytotoxic CD56dim NK cells characterized by robust expression of the complete cytotoxic granule machinery including perforin, granzymes, and granulysin. These cells are specialized for ADCC and direct target cell lysis through membrane pore formation and serine protease-mediated apoptosis.
key_evidence: PRF1: Pore-forming protein essential for granule-mediated cytolysis, top-ranked marker of cytotoxic NK phenotype
GZMB/GZMA: Serine proteases that induce target apoptosis; granzyme B particularly enriched in CD56dim effector NK cells
GNLY: Antimicrobial granulysin co-packaged in cytotoxic granules, released upon NK activation
FCGR3A: CD16 marker defining CD56dim NK population; enables ADCC via Fc receptor engagement
KLRF1/KLRD1/TYROBP: Activating receptors and ITAM-bearing adaptor supporting cytotoxic synapse formation
suggested_validation: Sort bone marrow CD56dim (CD16+CD56-) and CD56bright (CD16-CD56++) NK cells, confirm feature enrichment in CD56dim subset, and correlate with perforin degranulation assays and ADCC capacity.

functional_description: This feature represents mature, peripherally-distributed NK cells with potent cytotoxic machinery and antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) capacity. The signature is dominated by granzymes (GZMB, GZMA), perforin, and granulysin—hallmarks of CD56dim NK cells primed for target cell killing. High FCGR3A expression (CD16) enables IgG-mediated activation, while activating lectin-like receptors (KLRF1, KLRD1/CD94) coordinate cytotoxic responses.
key_evidence: GZMB/GZMA/PRF1: Classical cytotoxic triad—serine proteases and pore-forming protein essential for target cell apoptosis in mature CD56dim cells
GNLY: Granulysin antimicrobial protein co-packed in cytotoxic granules with granzymes; marker of differentiated effector NK phenotype
FCGR3A: CD16 expression defines CD56dim subset; mediates ADCC and responds to antibody-opsonized targets
NKG7: NK granule protein involved in cytotoxic synapse formation; highly restricted to activated cytotoxic lymphocytes
TYROBP/FCER1G: ITAM-bearing signaling adaptor associated with activating receptors (KIR and NKG2D); critical for cytotoxic signal transduction
suggested_validation: Sort bone marrow NK cells on CD56/CD16 expression and validate enrichment of this signature in CD56dim/CD16+ population by flow cytometry; confirm functional cytotoxicity via standard NK cell killing assay.

functional_description: This feature represents a highly activated cytotoxic NK cell state characterized by the coordinated expression of the complete cytolytic granule machinery and their supporting signaling apparatus. The programme is dominated by perforin-granzyme-mediated cytotoxicity with granulysin antimicrobial activity, supported by adaptor proteins and chemokine secretion for immune recruitment.
key_evidence: GNLY: Saposin-like granulysin protein marking cytotoxic granule content with antimicrobial function
PRF1, GZMB, GZMA, CTSW: Complete cytotoxic serine protease and perforin pore-formation machinery for target cell lysis
TYROBP: ITAM-containing signaling adaptor enabling KIR/activating receptor signal transduction for cytotoxicity triggering
KLRF1, KLRD1: Activating NKG2C-like and CD94 C-type lectin receptors driving NK activation and cytokine release
NKG7, CD63: Granule membrane proteins and degranulation markers indicating active cytolytic preparation
suggested_validation: Sort feature-high vs feature-low NK cells and perform degranulation assays (CD107a upregulation) and cytotoxic killing assays against K562 targets to confirm functional cytotoxicity capacity.

functional_description: This signature represents quiescent regulatory T cells (Tregs) in a homeostatic, non-activated state, characterized by basal metabolic activity and cytoskeletal remodeling rather than active suppression or proliferation. The dominant CD4 Regulatory enrichment (48%) combined with actin dynamics genes and mitochondrial function genes suggests Tregs maintaining immune tolerance through stable, low-energy cellular states.
key_evidence: CD27: TNF-receptor superfamily member essential for T cell immunity and Treg maintenance
TMSB4X, ACTG1, COTL1: Actin-binding proteins controlling cytoskeletal dynamics for Treg trafficking and stability
UCP2, MT-CO2, MT-CO3, NDUFB9: Mitochondrial uncoupling and OXPHOS components supporting regulated metabolic quiescence
ISG20: Interferon-stimulated exonuclease suggests antiviral sensing capability of Treg compartment
GZMK: Granzyme K indicates subset with suppressive potential within regulatory compartment
suggested_validation: Perform flow cytometry validation using CD4+CD27+FOXP3+ gating on feature-positive cells and measure mitochondrial membrane potential (TMRM/JC-1 staining) to confirm quiescent metabolic state in Tregs.

functional_description: This feature represents highly activated NK cells with robust cytotoxic granule machinery and ITAM-dependent signaling. The dominant expression of GNLY, NKG7, and CTSW alongside TYROBP signaling adaptor indicates cells primed for immediate cytolytic function, with prominent CD56bright NK representation suggesting activated bone marrow-resident or recently stimulated NK populations.
key_evidence: GNLY: Central cytotoxic granule protein with antimicrobial and cytolytic activity, hallmark of activated NK cells
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor mediating KIR and activating receptor signal transduction in NK cells
NKG7 + CTSW: Cytotoxic granule-associated proteins coordinating perforin-mediated killing machinery
KLRD1 + KLRF1: CD94/NKG2 and NKp80 activating receptors driving NK cytotoxicity and cytokine release
IL2RB: IL-2 receptor beta chain reflecting IL-2 responsiveness characteristic of activated CD56bright NK cells
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining for CD56, CD57/KLRG1, perforin, and granzyme B expression combined with functional cytotoxicity assays to confirm activated cytotoxic NK phenotype.

functional_description: This feature represents mature, activated NK cells with maximal cytotoxic effector function characterized by robust expression of the complete cytotoxic granule arsenal (perforin, granzymes A/B, granulysin). The dominance of NKG7 and coordinated upregulation of serine proteases, cysteine proteases, and pore-forming proteins indicates NK cells primed for immediate target cell killing.
key_evidence: NKG7: Rank #1 marker, integral plasma membrane NK granule protein essential for cytotoxic degranulation machinery
PRF1/GZMB/GZMA/GNLY: Complete cytotoxic effector arsenal with perforin pore formation and granzyme-mediated apoptosis induction
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor coupling KIR and activating receptor signaling to downstream cytotoxic activation
KLRF1/KLRD1/KLRB1: Mature NK cell activating and regulatory C-type lectin receptors defining CD56dim cytotoxic phenotype
CST7/CTSW/FGFBP2: Specialized proteases and cytokine-binding proteins supporting sustained cytolytic activity
suggested_validation: Sort NK cells by CD56dim/KIR+ phenotype and correlate with flow cytometry for PRF1/GZMB co-expression and CD57 maturation marker to confirm activated peripheral NK cytotoxic sub-programme.

programme_name: Cytotoxic effector NK cell granule machinery
functional_description: This feature represents mature, highly cytotoxic NK cells with abundant granule proteins and lytic machinery. The signature is dominated by perforin, granzymes, and granule-associated proteins that mediate direct target cell killing, characteristic of activated effector NK cells.
key_evidence: PRF1: Perforin is essential for forming membrane pores enabling granzyme delivery and cytolysis
GZMA: Granzyme A is a serine protease critical for NK-mediated target cell lysis
NKG7: Natural killer granule protein 7 is a granule component enriched in cytotoxic NK cells
CTSW: Cathepsin W is an NK-specific cysteine proteinase involved in cytolytic mechanisms
KLRF1: NKp80 activating receptor stimulates cytotoxicity and cytokine release in effector NK cells
suggested_validation: Sort CD56dim vs CD56bright NK subsets and validate PRF1/GZMA/NKG7 protein expression by flow cytometry alongside functional cytotoxicity assays (CFSE killing or CD107a degranulation).

functional_description: This feature represents mature, highly cytotoxic NK cells characterized by robust granule-mediated killing machinery and ADCC capacity. The signature is dominated by perforin, granzymes (A/B), and granulysin - core executors of target cell lysis - along with activating receptors (NKG7, KLRF1) and FcγRIIIa for antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity.
key_evidence: PRF1, GZMB, GZMA, GNLY: Complete cytotoxic granule apparatus for CD56dim effector function
FCGR3A (CD16): Signature marker of peripheral CD56dim NK cells enabling ADCC
TYROBP (DAP12): ITAM-containing adaptor coupling KIR and activating receptors to cytotoxic signaling
KLRF1 (NKp80), KLRD1 (CD94): Activating C-type lectin receptors driving cytotoxicity
CST7, CTSW, FGFBP2: Granule proteases and cytotoxic lymphocyte-specific factors supporting lytic capacity
suggested_validation: Sort CD56dim/CD16+ NK cells and verify co-expression of PRF1, GZMB, and FCGR3A using flow cytometry or qPCR; correlate feature activation with ADCC and perforin-dependent target cell killing assays.

functional_description: This feature represents activated cytotoxic NK cells with robust granule exocytosis machinery and immediate effector function. The signature is dominated by cytotoxic granule proteins (NKG7, GNLY, CTSW, CST7) and signaling adapters (TYROBP, FCER1G) that coordinate NK cell-mediated killing, with strong enrichment in both CD56high (39%) and CD56dim (36%) NK populations indicating a pan-NK cytotoxic state.
key_evidence: NKG7: NK granule protein essential for cytotoxic synapse organization and granule exocytosis
GNLY: Granulysin antimicrobial cytotoxin released from granules upon target cell engagement
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adapter for KIR and NKG2 receptors enabling activation signal transduction
CTSW: Cysteine protease in cytotoxic granules regulating NK-mediated target cell lysis
KLRF1: Activating NK receptor stimulating cytotoxicity and coordinating granule release machinery
suggested_validation: Confirm with flow cytometry measuring CD107a degranulation, perforin/granzyme intracellular staining, and functional killing assays to validate the cytotoxic effector phenotype.

functional_description: This feature represents a bone marrow-resident CD56bright NK cell sub-programme characterized by active cytotoxic granule biogenesis and trafficking. The signature reflects functional NK cells with elevated expression of cytotoxic effector molecules (granzymes, granulysin, cathepsin W) coupled with signaling adaptor proteins (TYROBP, FCER1G) and NK cell receptors (KLRF1, KLRD1, KLRB1) necessary for target recognition and granule exocytosis.
key_evidence: TYROBP: ITAM-bearing signaling adaptor required for KIR and activating NK receptor signal transduction
GNLY & GZMA: Core cytotoxic granule proteins mediating target cell lysis
KLRF1: Activating homodimeric C-type lectin receptor stimulating NK cytotoxicity
NKG7 & CD63: Granule membrane proteins essential for cytotoxic granule trafficking and exocytosis
IL2RB: β-chain of IL-2 receptor enabling survival and proliferation signals in bone marrow niche
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry co-staining CD56bright NK cells with CD63/NKG7 (granule markers) and intracellular GZMA/GNLY content, plus confirm TYROBP-KIR association in matched KIR+ CD56bright subsets.

programme_name: CD8 effector memory cytotoxic granule programme
functional_description: This feature represents activated CD8 effector memory T cells with enhanced cytotoxic capacity, characterized by robust expression of serine proteases (granzymes A, B, H) and cytolytic granule proteins. The signature reflects antigen-experienced cells equipped for direct target cell killing and chemokine-mediated recruitment of additional immune cells to inflammatory sites.
key_evidence: GZMB, GZMA, GZMH: Serine proteases essential for perforin-independent target cell apoptosis; hallmark of activated cytotoxic lymphocytes
GNLY, CST7: Cytotoxic granule-associated proteins; granulysin has antimicrobial activity against intracellular pathogens
CCL5: Chemokine secretion programme; major HIV-suppressive factor produced by CD8+ cells; recruits memory T helpers and monocytes
NKG7, FGFBP2, CTSW: Granule-associated effector molecules; cysteine protease with IL-2-responsive regulation indicating recent activation
TYROBP, KLRD1: Signalling adaptors and NK-lineage markers; ITAM-containing proteins supporting sustained effector function
suggested_validation: Sort CD8+CD45RA-CCR7- effector memory cells and confirm co-expression of GZMB, CCL5, and GNLY by flow cytometry or qPCR to validate the cytotoxic activation state.

functional_description: This feature captures the cytotoxic granule exocytosis programme characteristic of activated CD8 effector memory T cells and NK cells. The signature is dominated by perforin, granzymes (A, B, H), and granulysin—the core effector molecules mediating target cell killing. These cells represent recently antigen-exposed or tissue-resident cytotoxic lymphocytes with immediate cytolytic capacity.
key_evidence: PRF1, GZMA, GZMB, GZMH: Core pore-forming and serine protease components of the cytotoxic granule exocytosis pathway, the defining mechanism of cytotoxic T cells and NK cells
GNLY: Granulysin localizes to cytotoxic granules and is released upon antigen stimulation; antimicrobial activity indicates activated state
NKG7, KLRD1, KLRF1: NK cell-specific activation markers and lectin-like receptors; NKG7 is a canonical NK/CD8 effector memory signature gene
CTSW, CST7: Cysteine protease and inhibitor supporting the cytotoxic granule machinery; CTSW upregulated by IL-2 in activated cytotoxic cells
FCGR3A: NK cell and CD8 effector memory marker enabling antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) in activated state
suggested_validation: Sort CD8 effector memory and NK cells, then co-stain with surface markers (CD45RA−, CCR7−, FCGR3A+) and intracellular perforin/granzyme B to confirm the cytotoxic activation state in the SAE-defined population.

programme_name: Activated cytotoxic NK cell granule program
functional_description: This feature represents the core cytotoxic effector machinery of activated NK cells, dominated by the complete repertoire of granule-associated cytolytic proteins (perforin, granzymes A/B, granulysin) and their supporting signaling infrastructure. The signature reflects mature, peripherally-distributed CD56dim NK cells engaged in direct target cell killing, characterized by 76% NK cell enrichment and exceptional activation specificity (47-fold enrichment).
key_evidence: GZMB/GZMA/GNLY/PRF1: All four core cytotoxic granule proteins present—complete killing machinery for pore formation and apoptosis induction
NKG7: Canonical NK granule marker and most strongly NK-enriched gene; integral plasma membrane component essential for granule trafficking
TYROBP: ITAM-containing adapter coupling activating receptors (KIRs, NKG2D, KLRF1) to intracellular signaling cascades required for cytotoxicity
KLRD1/KLRF1: CD94 inhibitory checkpoint and NKp80 activating receptor—mature NK cell activation receptor panel in balanced configuration
CST7/CTSW: Cysteine protease inhibitors co-localized in granules; regulate protease activity and support sustained cytolytic function
suggested_validation: Perform flow cytometry on bone marrow NK cells using markers CD56/CD16/CD57, costain with NKG7, PRF1, and GZMB to confirm CD56dim phenotype and validate granule protein co-expression in activated NK populations.

functional_description: This feature represents mature, highly cytotoxic NK cells with robust granule-mediated killing machinery. The signature is dominated by canonical cytotoxicity genes (PRF1, GZMB, GNLY) and activating receptors (KLRF1, FCGR3A), characteristic of CD56dim peripheral NK cells optimized for target cell elimination.
key_evidence: PRF1: Perforin pore-formation machinery essential for granule-mediated cytotoxicity in CD56dim cells
GZMB: Granzyme B serine protease for target cell apoptosis, hallmark of cytotoxic differentiation
GNLY: Granulysin antimicrobial protein stored in lytic granules of mature cytotoxic NK cells
FCGR3A: CD16 mediates antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity, defining CD56dim NK subset
KLRF1: NKp80 activating receptor stimulates cytotoxicity and inflammatory cytokine release
suggested_validation: Sort CD56dim vs CD56bright NK cells and validate elevated expression of this signature in CD56dim subset using flow cytometry and functional killing assays.

functional_description: This feature represents terminally differentiated, cytotoxically competent NK cells with a mature effector phenotype. The signature is dominated by core cytotoxic machinery genes (PRF1, GZMB, GZMA, GNLY, CTSW) alongside NK-specific activation receptors and signaling adapters, indicating cells poised for immediate target cell killing.
key_evidence: PRF1, GZMB, GZMA, GNLY: Complete cytotoxic granule proteome for perforin-granzyme killing pathway
TYROBP (DAP12): ITAM-containing signaling adaptor required for activating KIR and NKG2 receptor signaling
KLRF1 (NKp80): Constitutively expressed activating C-type lectin receptor driving cytotoxicity
NKG7, CST7, FGFBP2: NK cell-specific cytotoxic granule proteins and secretory products
KLRD1 (CD94), KLRB1 (NKp65): Mature NK cell-associated C-type lectin receptors
suggested_validation: Sort CD56dim NK cells by FACS and confirm high co-expression of PRF1+GZMB+KLRF1+ phenotype with flow cytometry; validate cytotoxic function via standard NK killing assays.

programme_name: CD8 effector memory cytotoxic granule programme
functional_description: This signature represents activated CD8+ effector memory T cells with strong cytotoxic capacity, characterized by high expression of granule-associated serine proteases (granzymes A, B, H), perforin, and cytotoxic effector molecules. The programme is enriched for cells actively engaged in target cell killing and inflammatory chemokine secretion (CCL5), consistent with recently activated or antigen-experienced cytotoxic lymphocytes.
key_evidence: GZMB, GZMA, GZMH: Core serine proteases mediating target cell apoptosis; granzymes are hallmark of activated cytotoxic T cells
PRF1: Perforin forms membrane pores essential for granzyme delivery; fundamental to cytolytic function
CCL5: HIV-suppressive chemokine produced by CD8+ cells; recruits memory T cells and monocytes to inflammatory sites
GNLY, CTSW, CST7: Additional granule-associated proteases and cysteine protease inhibitors supporting cytotoxic granule biology
Cell composition 72.5% CD8 Effector Memory 2: Direct validation that signature is dominated by CD8 effector memory subset
suggested_validation: Sort CD8+ T cells by CCL5 and GZMB expression and confirm high cytotoxic capacity via FACS-based perforin/granzyme analysis or functional killing assays against target cells.

functional_description: This feature represents a quiescent regulatory T cell programme dominated by housekeeping and basal metabolic processes rather than active immunosuppression. The signature is enriched for cytoskeletal maintenance (TMSB4X, ACTG1, COTL1), mitochondrial function (UCP2, MT-CO2), and protein quality control (UBB), reflecting steady-state Treg homoeostasis in bone marrow.
key_evidence: CD27: TNF-receptor superfamily member essential for long-term T cell immunity; marks memory-competent T cells including Tregs
TMSB4X + ACTG1 + COTL1: Actin-binding proteins driving cytoskeletal dynamics required for T cell trafficking and baseline motility
UCP2 + MT-CO2: Mitochondrial uncoupling and oxidative phosphorylation; supports metabolic flexibility in quiescent regulatory cells
CD74: MHC-II chaperone and MIF receptor; marks antigen-experienced and activated regulatory T cells
LAT + TRAC: TCR signalling components present but not hyperactivated; indicates mature, antigen-educated Treg population
suggested_validation: Sort CD4+CD25+FOXP3+ Tregs from bone marrow and confirm this signature is enriched in non-proliferating (Ki67−) cells with UCP2+ and TMSB4X+ protein expression by flow cytometry.

functional_description: This feature represents highly activated NK cells with maximal cytotoxic effector function, characterized by expression of the complete cytotoxic granule proteome (granzymes A/B, granulysin, cathepsin W) and signaling machinery for cytotoxic synapse formation. The 50.5% representation of CD56bright cells alongside canonical cytotoxic markers suggests a population of bone marrow-resident or activated NK cells poised for immediate target cell lysis.
key_evidence: GNLY, GZMA, GZMB: Complete cytotoxic granule protease arsenal for perforin-independent and -dependent target apoptosis
CTSW, CST7: Cathepsin W and cystatin F form regulatory pair controlling protease activity within cytotoxic granules
TYROBP, FCER1G: ITAM-bearing adapter proteins enabling signal transduction through activating NK receptors (KIRs, NKG2D pathway)
KLRF1, KLRD1: Activating NKp80 receptor and CD94/NKG2 inhibitory checkpoint, indicating mature receptor repertoire
NKG7, CD63: Granule membrane and secretory vesicle trafficking proteins marking active degranulation competence
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of CD56bright/dim with GZMB, perforin, and CD94/NKG2A/C; functional assays measuring target cell lysis and granule exocytosis in sorted populations.

functional_description: This feature represents actively proliferating cytotoxic T cells with robust effector functions, characterized by high expression of cytotoxic granule proteins (PRF1, CTSW, NKG7), chemokine production (CCL5), and metabolic activation. The dominant composition of T Proliferating cells (46.5%) with CD8 Effector Memory cells (16%) indicates antigen-driven clonal expansion coupled with immediate cytolytic capacity.
key_evidence: PRF1: Perforin mediates target cell lysis through pore formation, essential for cytotoxic T cell function
CCL5: Major chemokine produced by activated CD8+ T cells for immune cell recruitment and HIV suppression
CTSW: Cathepsin W is upregulated by IL-2 and specifically expressed in cytotoxic T cells for proteolytic granule function
NKG7: Natural killer granule protein marks cells with active cytotoxic granule mobilization machinery
STMN1 + MT-CO2: Microtubule destabilization and mitochondrial oxidative metabolism indicate rapid cell division and high energetic demand
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry co-staining for CD8, Ki-67 (proliferation), and intracellular granzyme B/perforin to confirm the cytotoxic proliferating T cell phenotype.

programme_name: Proliferating T cells with elevated mitochondrial metabolism
functional_description: This feature represents actively proliferating T cells with markedly upregulated oxidative phosphorylation and mitochondrial respiration capacity. The signature is dominated by mitochondrial electron transport chain components (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, NDUFB9, COX5A) alongside proliferation-associated cytoskeletal remodeling (TMSB4X, ACTG1) and chromatin accessibility factors (HMGN2, H3F3A). This metabolic signature supports the high ATP demands of rapid cell division.
key_evidence: MT-CO3, MT-CO2, MT-ND1: Complex I and IV components indicate enhanced mitochondrial respiration required for proliferating T cell energy demands
NDUFB9, COX5A: Additional electron transport chain subunits reinforce oxidative phosphorylation upregulation in dividing cells
TMSB4X, ACTG1: Actin-binding and cytoskeletal proteins essential for cytokinesis and cell migration during proliferation
HMGN2: Nucleosomal binding protein associated with transcriptionally active chromatin supporting proliferation-associated gene expression
IL32: T cell activation cytokine upregulated during mitogen-driven T cell proliferation, validating activated proliferating phenotype
suggested_validation: Validate using Ki-67 staining or FUCCI cell cycle reporter combined with Seahorse extracellular flux analysis to confirm mitochondrial respiration is elevated in the top-200 feature-activated cells compared to resting T cells.

functional_description: This feature captures actively proliferating regulatory T cells (Tregs) with elevated metabolic activity and cytoskeletal reorganization. The dominance of CD4 Regulatory (44.5%) and T Proliferating (48.0%) cells, combined with high expression of actin-binding proteins and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation components, indicates Tregs undergoing homeostatic proliferation in bone marrow niche rather than activated effector differentiation.
key_evidence: TMSB4X, ACTG1, COTL1: Actin-sequestering and cytoskeletal remodeling proteins essential for cell division and migration during proliferation
IL32: Cytokine upregulated upon T cell activation and particularly in regulatory T cell lineages; promotes homeostatic rather than inflammatory responses
MT-CO2, NDUFB9, UCP2: Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and ATP synthesis genes indicating high metabolic demand of proliferating cells
TRAC: Consistently expressed as baseline T cell receptor identity marker across all T cell populations
NOP10, HMGN2: Nucleolar and chromatin-associated proteins supporting increased ribosomal biogenesis and transcription during S/G2 phases of cell cycle
suggested_validation: Sort CD4+FOXP3+Ki67+ regulatory T cells from bone marrow and perform qPCR validation of metabolic genes (NDUFB9, UCP2) and actin regulators (TMSB4X, ACTG1) to confirm Treg-specific proliferation signature.

functional_description: This feature captures a metabolic and translational programme characteristic of actively engaged cytotoxic T cells and NK cells, marked by elevated mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) genes and ribosomal protein expression supporting rapid protein synthesis. The co-enrichment of CTSW and GNLY with metabolic machinery suggests cells poised for or actively executing cytotoxic granule-mediated killing, requiring substantial ATP and protein production.
key_evidence: MT-CO3, MT-CO2, MT-ND5: Mitochondrial electron transport chain complex subunits indicating elevated OXPHOS metabolism for energy-demanding cytotoxic functions
CTSW: Cathepsin W directly involved in T-cell cytolytic activity and enriched in cytotoxic granules
GNLY: Granulysin located in cytotoxic granules of CTLs and NK cells, released upon antigen stimulation
RPS24, RPL37A, RPLP0, RPS2, RPS23, RPS17: Ribosomal proteins supporting high protein synthesis capacity for rapid granule and effector molecule production
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain for iron homeostasis during metabolically active states
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry quantifying perforin/granzyme content and surface CD107a (LAMP1) degranulation capacity in top-expressing cells, with metabolic profiling (SEAHORSE) confirming OXPHOS dominance over glycolysis.

functional_description: This feature represents terminally differentiated, cytotoxically-armed NK cells enriched for granule-mediated killing machinery. The signature is dominated by perforin and multiple granzymes (GZMB, GZMH, GZMA) alongside granulysin, reflecting a mature cytotoxic phenotype characteristic of peripheral CD56dim NK cells. Co-expression of activating receptors (KLRF1, KLRD1/CD94) and TYROBP-mediated signaling indicates poised cytotoxic readiness with enhanced killing capacity.
key_evidence: PRF1, GZMB, GZMH, GZMA, GNLY: Complete cytotoxic granule protein arsenal defining CD56dim effector function
NKG7, CST7, CTSW, FGFBP2: Specialized cytolytic mediators selectively expressed by mature cytotoxic NK cells
TYROBP: ITAM-bearing adaptor enabling KIR signaling and activating receptor-mediated cytotoxicity
KLRF1, KLRD1: Activating receptors poised for target recognition and cytotoxic degranulation
CCL5: Chemokine production capacity supporting recruitment and local immune amplification at cytotoxic sites
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry gating on CD56dim/CD57+/KLRD1+/NKG2A- cells with intracellular staining for PRF1, GZMB, and GNLY should confirm this represents mature peripheral cytotoxic NK cells enriched in this SAE feature.

functional_description: This feature represents activated cytotoxic lymphocytes (CD8 effector memory and NK cells) with elevated mitochondrial oxidative metabolism supporting high-demand cytotoxic granule production and secretion. The programme is characterized by expression of cytolytic proteins (GZMB, GNLY, NKG7, CTSW) and chemokines (CCL5) alongside bioenergetic genes enabling sustained cytotoxic function.
key_evidence: GZMB, GNLY, NKG7, CTSW: serine proteases and granule proteins mediating target cell apoptosis in activated cytotoxic lymphocytes
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-ND5: mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes I and IV subunits supporting ATP-intensive cytotoxic granule exocytosis
CCL5: major chemokine produced by activated CD8+ effector memory cells for recruitment of additional immune cells
CD8 Effector Memory 2 (20%) and NK (25.5%) dominant in top-200 activating cells with 52x enrichment fold-change
TYROBP, KLRD1, CST7: immune signaling adaptors and regulators consistent with active NK and CTL receptor engagement
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of bone marrow T cells for CD8/CCR7/CD45RA phenotyping combined with perforin/granzyme B intracellular staining to confirm effector memory activation state and functional cytotoxic capacity.

functional_description: This feature represents a T cell sub-programme dominated by ribosomal protein biogenesis and translational machinery activation, characteristic of metabolically active cells undergoing homeostatic proliferation. The enrichment across naive, central memory, and effector memory CD4 T cells suggests this reflects basal protein synthesis capacity rather than antigen-driven activation, with accessory signals from LTB and iron metabolism supporting survival and proliferation.
key_evidence: RPS26, RPS23, RPS17, RPS2, RPL7A, RPL4, RPL37A: Constitute 7 of top 10 genes; 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit proteins indicating active translation machinery
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor supporting sustained protein synthesis capacity
LTB: Lymphotoxin-beta expression suggests TNF superfamily signaling supporting homeostatic T cell survival and proliferation
FTH1, LDHB: Iron storage and glycolytic metabolism markers consistent with metabolic demands of proliferating cells
Balanced distribution across naive/CM/EM (75.5% CD4): Indicates housekeeping translation programme across multiple maturation states rather than differentiation-specific activation
suggested_validation: Sort top-200 cells by proliferation markers (Ki-67, MKI67) and cell cycle phase (S/G2M) to confirm elevated ribosomal protein expression correlates with active cell division independent of TCR activation status.

functional_description: This feature represents a T cell sub-programme characterized by elevated ribosomal and translation machinery genes, indicating heightened protein synthesis capacity. The dominance of CD4 naive cells (41.5%) combined with high activation in proliferating T cells (6.5%) suggests homeostatic proliferation rather than antigen-driven activation, consistent with naive T cell expansion in lymphoid niches.
key_evidence: RPS2, RPL4, RPS23, RPS24, RPL7A, RPLP0, RPL37A, RPS26: All ribosomal protein subunits (40S and 60S) indicating active protein synthesis machinery
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor required for aminoacyl-tRNA delivery to ribosomes during sustained protein synthesis
LDHB: Glycolytic enzyme supporting energy metabolism during anabolic proliferation
LTB: Lymphotoxin-beta expression in naive cells consistent with lymphoid tissue homeostasis and secondary lymphoid organ development
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein supporting mRNA processing during high-throughput translation
suggested_validation: Sort CD4 naive vs CD4 effector memory T cells and measure ribosomal biogenesis rate via qPCR of RPS2/RPL4 combined with Ki-67 staining to confirm proliferation without antigen-driven activation markers (granzyme B, IFN-γ).

programme_name: CD8 effector memory cytotoxic granule programme
functional_description: This feature represents activated CD8+ effector memory T cells with robust cytotoxic capacity, characterized by high expression of granzymes (GZMA, GZMH), perforin (PRF1), and cytolytic proteases (CTSW). The signature reflects cells primed for immediate target cell lysis with chemokine production (CCL5) for immune cell recruitment, consistent with bone marrow-resident or recently activated effector memory populations.
key_evidence: GZMA, GZMH, PRF1: Core cytotoxic granule proteins enabling target cell apoptosis via perforin-granzyme pathway
CTSW: Serine protease specifically upregulated in cytotoxic T lymphocytes for cytolytic function
CCL5: HIV-suppressive chemokine secreted by activated CD8+ cells; recruits memory T cells and monocytes
CD8A + NKG7: Defines CD8+ effector memory cells with natural killer-like cytotoxic capacity
FGFBP2: Selectively secreted by cytotoxic lymphocytes; marker of cytotoxic differentiation
suggested_validation: Sort CD8+NKG7+ cells from bone marrow and validate granzyme production by intracellular flow cytometry with functional killing assays on target cells to confirm cytotoxic capacity.

functional_description: This feature represents actively proliferating T cells with elevated metabolic demands, characterized by upregulation of ribosomal proteins, mitochondrial respiratory chain components, and cytoskeletal dynamics. The signature reflects anabolic processes and energy production required for rapid cell division, with particular enrichment in T Proliferating cells (49.5%) and secondary representation of effector memory populations.
key_evidence: RPS24, RPS26, RPS2: Ribosomal protein components enabling enhanced protein synthesis during active proliferation
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, UQCRQ: Mitochondrial respiratory chain subunits supporting oxidative phosphorylation for ATP generation in dividing cells
TMSB4X: Actin sequestering protein regulating cytoskeletal remodeling during cell division and migration
IL32: Cytokine upregulated after T cell mitogenic activation; mediates inflammatory responses in proliferating populations
HMGN2, H3F3A: Histone variants and nucleosome-associated proteins facilitating transcriptionally active chromatin remodeling in proliferating cells

functional_description: This feature represents a canonical cytotoxic NK cell programme dominated by pre-formed granule proteins essential for target cell lysis. programme_name: Memory T cell calcium signaling and survival
functional_description: This feature represents a programme enriched in CD4 memory (central and effector) and regulatory T cells characterized by elevated calcium-binding proteins (S100 family, galectins) and IL-32 cytokine expression. programme_name: Naive T cell high protein synthesis
functional_description: This feature represents a metabolically active naive T cell state characterized by elevated ribosomal protein expression and hemoglobin transcripts, indicating high translational capacity and active protein synthesis machinery. The enrichment in CD8 and CD4 naive cells (92.5% of top activators) with 18.31-fold elevation suggests these cells are primed for rapid proliferation and differentiation upon antigen encounter.

MT-CO2, MT-CO3: Mitochondrial respiratory chain components reflect elevated oxidative metabolism supporting proliferation

functional_description: This feature captures a highly active ribosomal and translational machinery programme enriched in naive T cells from bone marrow, reflecting elevated protein synthesis capacity required for homeostatic proliferation and metabolic activity. The dominance of ribosomal proteins (RPS, RPL series), translation elongation factors (EEF1B2), and nucleolar assembly factors (NPM1) indicates active mRNA translation and cell growth rather than antigen-driven activation or quiescence.

RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0: 60S ribosomal subunit components—assembled ribosome abundance correlates with protein synthesis capacity

NPM1: Nucleophosmin involved in ribosomal protein chaperoning and cell proliferation signalling
Naive cell enrichment (81% CD4/CD8 naive): Homeostatic proliferation in naive T cells requires sustained protein synthesis for TCR signalling, cytokine receptor expression, and IL-7-driven survival
suggested_validation: Correlate with cell cycle markers (MKI67, PCNA) and IL-7 signalling intermediates; validate via polysome profiling or O-propargyl-puromycin (OPP) incorporation assays in sorted naive bone marrow T cells.

programme_name: Naive T cell protein synthesis homeostasis
functional_description: This feature captures a core translational machinery programme enriched in naive CD4 and CD8 T cells, characterized by robust ribosomal protein expression and translation elongation factors. The signature reflects the basal protein synthesis capacity required for cellular homeostasis and rapid response capability in quiescent naive T cells, not antigen-driven activation.

NPM1, HNRNPA1: Nucleolar chaperones and RNA-binding proteins involved in ribosomal biogenesis and mRNA processing

programme_name: CD4 effector memory with regulatory plasticity
functional_description: This feature represents activated CD4+ effector memory T cells with concurrent regulatory T cell characteristics, marked by elevated S100 calcium-binding proteins and IL-32 cytokine expression. TRAC: T cell receptor alpha constant chain, confirms T cell lineage and TCR expression
Ribosomal proteins (RPLP0, RPS17, RPL4, RPL37A, RPS2): Active protein synthesis capacity supporting sustained cytokine and effector molecule production
LTB: Lymphotoxin-beta mediates inflammatory TNF-family signaling, consistent with activated effector memory phenotype

functional_description: This feature represents a basal translational and ribosomal biogenesis programme active in naive and central memory CD4 T cells during homeostatic proliferation in bone marrow. The signature is dominated by ribosomal proteins, translation factors, and nucleolar processing machinery, indicating active but non-inflammatory protein synthesis supporting cellular growth and division without antigen-driven activation.

FTH1: Iron storage protein suggesting metabolic support for proliferating cells undergoing active translation
PTMA: Prothymosin alpha protects against apoptosis and supports cell survival during proliferation
SOCS3: Cytokine-inducible inhibitor present despite lack of inflammatory cytokine genes, indicating basal immune tolerance in homeostatic state

programme_name: CD4 regulatory T cell homeostatic program
functional_description: This feature represents a quiescent, non-activated regulatory T cell programme dominated by CD4 Tregs (34.5%) and central memory cells with established immune tolerance functions. The signature reflects baseline homeostatic maintenance rather than active immune activation, with enrichment for cytoskeletal regulators and minimal inflammatory cytokine expression.

LTB + ISG20: Lymphotoxin-beta and interferon-responsive genes suggesting low-level basal inflammatory tone in established immune tolerance state

programme_name: Proliferating T cells homeostatic cell cycle
functional_description: This feature represents actively proliferating T cells characterized by elevated expression of genes supporting rapid cell division and protein synthesis. The signature is dominated by cytoskeletal regulators (TMSB4X, STMN1), nucleosomal proteins associated with active chromatin (HMGN1/2), and translational/RNA processing machinery (HNRNPA3, SNRPB), reflecting the biosynthetic demands of cell cycle progression.

STMN1: Microtubule destabilizer critical for mitotic spindle dynamics and cytokinesis
HMGN1/HMGN2: Active chromatin binding proteins maintaining open chromatin for transcription during S/G2 phases
IL32: Activation-induced cytokine expressed after T cell mitogenic stimulation, supports proliferation
CALM3: Calmodulin regulates cell cycle progression and cytokinesis via calcium signaling
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry validation of Ki-67 and phospho-histone H3 co-expression in TMSB4X+ cells, combined with metabolic profiling to confirm elevated mitochondrial respiration (IDH2, UQCRQ) in cycling populations.

functional_description: This feature represents T cells with an activated translational and secretory programme, characterized by abundant ribosomal proteins, immunoglobulin transcripts (IGKC, IGHA1), and metabolic support genes. The enrichment in CD4 naive and effector memory cells suggests antigen-driven differentiation toward a plasma cell-like phenotype, though this is atypical for T cells and may represent bystander activation or contamination with B cell transcripts in sorted T cell populations.

IGKC, IGHA1: Immunoglobulin transcripts suggest antibody secretion programme or cross-contamination with plasma cells
LTB: Lymphotoxin-beta mediates inflammatory signalling and lymphoid tissue development, supporting activated phenotype
PRDX2: Antioxidant enzyme supporting high metabolic activity and antiviral CD8 T cell function
LDHB, TMSB4X: Glycolytic enzyme and actin-regulatory protein supporting rapid proliferation and migration
suggested_validation: Perform in situ hybridization or flow cytometry to confirm whether IGKC/IGHA1 expression colocalizes with T cell markers or represents B cell contamination; validate translation rate via puromycin incorporation assay.

programme_name: CD4 central memory homeostatic protein synthesis
functional_description: This feature represents a homeostatic protein synthesis programme predominantly active in CD4 central memory T cells within the bone marrow. The signature is dominated by ribosomal proteins (RPL/RPS genes) and translation machinery components, indicating active but non-activated protein synthesis. The enrichment of ZFP36 (AU-rich element binding) and JUN suggests capacity for rapid post-transcriptional control in response to homeostatic or low-level stimulation.
key_evidence: RPL37A, RPS23, RPS2, RPL7A, RPLP0, RPS24, RPL4, RPS17: Core 60S/40S ribosomal subunit proteins indicating elevated basal translation
FTH1: Iron storage protein consistent with metabolically active but non-stressed cells
ZFP36: mRNA stability regulator enabling rapid cytokine response without active transcription
JUN: Immediate-early transcription factor involved in homeostatic proliferation signaling
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic protein supporting survival of long-lived memory cells

functional_description: This feature represents highly proliferative naive T cells, predominantly CD4 naive (53.5%) and CD8 naive (13.5%), characterized by elevated ribosomal protein synthesis and mitochondrial oxidative metabolism supporting rapid cell division. The signature reflects active protein translation machinery and bioenergetic demand typical of cells undergoing homeostatic proliferation rather than antigen-driven activation.
key_evidence: RPL7A, RPL4, RPS2, RPS24, RPS23, RPL37A, RPS17, RPS26: Coordinated upregulation of 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit proteins indicates active translational capacity for protein synthesis during proliferation
MT-CO3, MT-CO2, MT-ND1: Mitochondrial electron transport chain components suggest elevated oxidative phosphorylation supporting energy demands of rapidly dividing cells
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor required for efficient protein synthesis during active cell division
NPM1, HNRNPA1: Nucleolar and RNA-processing factors involved in ribosome biogenesis and mRNA processing during proliferation
DONSON: DNA replication fork stabilization factor supporting S-phase progression in dividing cells

functional_description: This feature represents a proliferative, metabolically active CD4 effector memory T cell programme dominated by ribosomal proteins and mitochondrial genes. MT-CO3, MT-ND1, MT-CO2: Mitochondrial respiratory chain components reflect elevated metabolic demand in activated effector cells

functional_description: This feature represents a technical artifact rather than a true T cell functional programme, characterized by high expression of ribosomal proteins and hemoglobin subunits. The dominant cell composition (59% CD4/CD8 naive) combined with robust hemoglobin gene expression (HBA1, HBA2, HBB, HBD) suggests bone marrow erythroid contamination or doublets during CITE-seq/scRNA-seq capture, rather than a biologically meaningful T cell state.

RPS26/RPS23/RPL37A/RPS17/RPL4: Constitutive ribosomal protein overexpression typical of highly translating erythroid precursors

suggested_validation: Cross-reference with erythroid/myeloid markers (CD34, GATA1, EPO) and confirm absence in CD45+ sorted T cell populations; verify contamination absent in quality-filtered analysis.

functional_description: This feature represents recently activated CD8 effector memory T cells engaged in cytotoxic function with active granule-mediated killing capacity. The signature is dominated by granzyme K (GZMK) combined with stress response and signal attenuation genes, indicating cells that have been stimulated and are rapidly executing effector functions while simultaneously dampening signal intensity to prevent over-activation.
key_evidence: GZMK: Serine protease essential for cytotoxic granule-mediated target cell lysis, hallmark of activated effector CD8 T cells
JUN: AP-1 transcription factor induced by TCR stimulation and cytokine signaling, drives effector differentiation and cytokine production
RGS1: Negative regulator of G-protein signaling that terminates chemokine and cytokine receptor signals, indicates signal resolution phase
DUSP2: Phosphatase that inactivates ERK/JNK MAP kinases, reflective of feedback inhibition following TCR/cytokine activation
CCL5: Chemokine produced by activated CD8 T cells, amplifies recruitment of additional immune cells to sites of infection
suggested_validation: Sort CD8 effector memory cells by GZMK/JUN expression and perform flow cytometry validation of cytotoxic granule content and intracellular phospho-ERK/phospho-JNK levels to confirm recently activated state.

programme_name: Proliferating T cells with high metabolic demand
functional_description: This feature represents actively proliferating T cells characterized by elevated mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and ribosomal protein expression, reflecting the substantial bioenergetic and synthetic demands of cell division. The dominance of T Proliferating cells (32%) and enrichment in CD4 Regulatory and CD4 Naive populations indicates a programme active across multiple T cell lineages during rapid expansion.

programme_name: Cytotoxic effector T cell activation programme
functional_description: This feature represents activated cytotoxic T cells with enhanced granule-mediated killing capacity. The signature is dominated by cytolytic proteases (GZMA, PRF1, CTSW), NK cell markers (NKG7), and pro-inflammatory mediators (IL32, CCL5) characteristic of recently activated CD8+ effector memory cells. The high enrichment in T Proliferating and CD8 Effector Memory 2 populations indicates antigen-driven clonal expansion with active cytotoxic function.

functional_description: This feature represents a contaminating or aberrant T cell population expressing hemoglobin subunits (HBA1, HBA2, HBB, HBD) and hemoglobin assembly factors (AHSP), alongside ribosomal proteins. programme_name: Proliferating T cells with elevated oxidative metabolism
functional_description: This feature captures actively proliferating T cells with enhanced mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and ATP production, supporting rapid biosynthesis and cell division. The signature is dominated by T Proliferating cells (37.5%) and CD4 Regulatory T cells (27%), both requiring high metabolic demand for anabolic processes and functional maintenance. The co-expression of mitochondrial electron transport chain components with proliferation-associated genes (TMSB4X, ribosomal proteins, IL32) indicates metabolic reprogramming driven by active cell cycling rather than TCR stimulation or effector function.

TMSB4X: Actin-sequestering protein regulating cytoskeletal dynamics essential for cell division and migration
RPS24, NOP10, HNRNPA1: Ribosomal and nucleolar proteins supporting rapid protein synthesis required during S/G2 phases
IL32: Cytokine upregulated upon T cell activation and proliferation, particularly in regulatory T cells
UCP2: Mitochondrial uncoupling protein reducing membrane potential; paradoxically involved in metabolic flexibility and proliferation regulation

programme_name: Proliferating T cells with homeostatic cell cycle
functional_description: This feature marks actively proliferating T cells characterized by elevated expression of cell cycle regulators, actin dynamics proteins, and mitochondrial metabolic machinery. TMSB4X: Actin sequestering protein regulating actin polymerization required for cytokinesis and cell migration during proliferation

PTMA/DEK: Nuclear regulators of DNA topology and mRNA processing supporting high transcriptional demand during proliferation

programme_name: IL-32 expressing regulatory T cell activation
functional_description: This feature represents activated regulatory T cells (Tregs) with elevated IL-32 cytokine expression, characterized by active chromatin remodeling and cellular proliferation. programme_name: CD4 effector memory active protein synthesis
functional_description: This feature represents a highly proliferative, protein synthesis-engaged state dominated by CD4 effector memory T cells in the bone marrow. EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor required for sustained protein synthesis during T cell activation and differentiation
LTB: Lymphotoxin-beta expressed on activated T cells, mediates inflammatory responses and lymphoid tissue remodeling
NPM1, YBX1, HNRNPA1: RNA/protein chaperones and processing factors supporting rapid biosynthesis during active proliferation

functional_description: This feature represents metabolically active CD4 central memory T cells with elevated oxidative phosphorylation and calcium-dependent signaling capacity. LMNA: Nuclear architecture gene essential for immune synapse formation and T cell activation memory
FTH1: Iron storage capacity reflecting quiescent but metabolically competent memory state

programme_name: Hemoglobin-expressing metabolically active memory T cells
functional_description: This feature represents CD4 central memory T cells with high expression of hemoglobin subunits (HBA1, HBA2, HBB, HBD, HBM) and ribosomal proteins, indicating active protein synthesis and metabolic engagement. programme_name: CD8 naive T cell with active protein synthesis
functional_description: This feature marks CD8 naive T cells characterized by elevated CD8A/B expression combined with increased ribosomal proteins and translation elongation factors, indicating heightened protein synthesis capacity. The enrichment in naive CD8 T cells (59%) and CD4 naive (22%) alongside metabolic markers (mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation genes) suggests cells preparing for or maintaining basal biosynthetic activity typical of quiescent lymphocytes ready for activation.

functional_description: This feature represents a CD56bright NK cell sub-programme characterized by robust cytotoxic granule biogenesis and maturation machinery. programme_name: Homeostatic proliferation in naive T cells
functional_description: This feature represents a proliferative programme characterized by upregulation of ribosomal proteins and translation factors, indicating active protein synthesis and cell cycle progression. The enrichment in CD4/CD8 naive cells (61% combined) combined with CD69 expression and cell cycle regulators (RGCC) suggests homeostatic proliferation rather than antigen-driven activation.

programme_name: CD8 effector memory cytotoxic granule programme
functional_description: This feature represents activated CD8 effector memory T cells with potent cytotoxic capacity, characterized by high expression of granzymes (GZMA, GZMB, GZMH), perforin, and cytolytic proteases. The concurrent upregulation of CCL4/CCL5 chemokines indicates these cells are actively secreting HIV-suppressive factors and recruiting additional immune cells to sites of infection or inflammation.

CCL4, CCL5, CCL3: HIV-suppressive chemokines produced by activated CD8+ effector cells

programme_name: Homeostatic protein synthesis and metabolic activity
functional_description: This feature represents a basal T cell metabolic state characterized by active ribosomal protein expression and translation machinery, indicating cells engaged in steady-state protein synthesis rather than activation-driven proliferation. The dominant composition of naive and central memory CD4 T cells suggests this programme maintains baseline anabolic capacity in quiescent or recently antigen-experienced cells.

programme_name: T cell proliferation and metabolic activation
functional_description: This feature represents actively proliferating T cells with elevated metabolic activity and TCR signaling capability. The signature is characterized by high expression of IL32 (inflammatory cytokine), core metabolic enzymes (ECH1, UCP2, NDUFB9), and cytoskeletal remodeling proteins (TMSB4X, S100A4/A6, ACTG1), reflecting rapid cell division and migration.

ECH1 + UCP2 + NDUFB9: Fatty acid oxidation and mitochondrial bioenergetics supporting high ATP demand of proliferating cells
suggested_validation: Sort Feature-1949-high cells and perform functional assays measuring BrdU/EdU incorporation, mitochondrial membrane potential (JC-1), and TCR-induced calcium flux to confirm active proliferation and TCR signaling capacity.

functional_description: This feature represents NK cells and γδ T cells with active cytotoxic granule machinery, characterized by high expression of cytolytic effector molecules (GNLY, CTSW, NKG7) and NK-lineage receptors (KLRB1, KLRC1, KLRD1, KLRF1). The programme is dominated by NK CD56high cells (49.5%) with a subset of activated CD4 naive cells (21%), likely representing natural killer T (NKT) cells or recently activated cytotoxic lymphocytes poised for immediate target killing.

KLRB1/KLRC1/KLRD1/KLRF1: C-type lectin receptors (NKG2 family, NKRP1), hallmark NK cell receptor repertoire

functional_description: This feature represents activated effector memory T cells with cytotoxic capacity, characterized by strong expression of chemokines (CCL5), cytotoxic granule proteins (GZMK, CTSW), and post-activation signaling regulation. The programme is dominated by CD8 effector memory cells (27.5%) with secondary CD4 central memory contribution, reflecting a circulating memory T cell population poised for rapid cytokine and cytotoxin delivery.

GZMK + CTSW: Serine proteases in cytotoxic granules; CTSW upregulated by IL-2 during T cell activation
MAP3K8: Activates TNF-alpha and IL-2 production during T lymphocyte activation; NF-kappaB pathway activation
DUSP2 + RGS1: Negative feedback regulators of MAPK/ERK and G-protein signaling; hallmark of post-activation signal termination
ZFP36: mRNA stability regulator for cytokine transcripts; involved in cellular response to cytokine stimulus
suggested_validation: Sort CD8 effector memory (CCR7-/CD45RA-) T cells and validate CCL5/GZMK co-expression alongside intracellular TNF-alpha and IFN-gamma production upon TCR stimulation.

functional_description: This feature represents a T cell sub-programme dominated by ribosomal proteins and translation machinery upregulation, indicating active protein synthesis and homeostatic proliferation. The signature is strongly enriched in CD4 naive T cells (53% of top activators), with secondary enrichment in central memory cells, characteristic of proliferating lymphocytes undergoing rapid growth and division in the bone marrow.

EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor supporting active protein synthesis during proliferation
TMSB4X: Actin regulation protein required for cell proliferation and cytoskeletal dynamics
LTB: Lymphotoxin-beta present in 53% CD4 naive cells, supporting TCR-independent homeostatic signaling
LDHB, NPM1, H3F3A: Metabolic and nucleolar proteins associated with cell cycle progression and proliferation
suggested_validation: Validate by sorting CD4 naive T cells from bone marrow and confirming elevated ribosomal protein expression via qPCR and flow cytometry analysis of proliferation markers (Ki-67, PCNA).

programme_name: CD4 central memory activation and proliferation
functional_description: This feature represents recently activated CD4 central memory T cells undergoing proliferation and metabolic reprogramming. The signature combines early activation markers (CD69, JUN) with iron homeostasis genes (FTH1, involved in managing oxidative stress during proliferation), cytokine signaling inhibitors (SOCS3), and actin dynamics regulators (TMSB4X) characteristic of cells transitioning from quiescence to active proliferation in the bone marrow niche.

TMSB4X: Actin sequesterer regulating cytoskeletal dynamics needed for cell migration and proliferation
suggested_validation: Sort CD4+ CD69+ cells from bone marrow and validate co-expression of FTH1, SOCS3, and JUN by flow cytometry or immunofluorescence to confirm the activated proliferating central memory phenotype.

programme_name: CD8 effector memory cytotoxic granule programme
functional_description: This feature captures activated CD8 effector memory T cells with high cytotoxic potential, characterized by abundant granzyme and perforin-related granule proteins (GZMA, GZMH, GZMK, CST7, CTSW) and chemokine secretion (CCL5). The programme reflects recently antigen-experienced cells undergoing active cytolytic function with elevated proliferation markers.

CCL5: Chemokine production characteristic of activated effector memory T cells recruiting other immune cells
CST7, CTSW: Cysteine protease inhibitors protecting cytotoxic machinery, upregulated by IL-2 activation
KLRG1: Terminal effector marker highly expressed in CD8 effector memory cells indicating late differentiation
CD8 Effector Memory 2 (30.5%) dominant: Direct annotation confirms this is mature cytotoxic effector population

programme_name: CD4 effector memory homeostatic protein synthesis
functional_description: This feature represents a heightened protein synthesis and translation programme predominantly expressed in CD4 effector memory T cells in bone marrow. The dominance of ribosomal proteins (40S and 60S subunits) and translation elongation factors indicates active protein production, likely supporting sustained cytokine production and metabolic demands characteristic of tissue-resident effector memory cells.

EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor supporting active mRNA translation during effector function
S100A4: Calcium-binding protein associated with cell motility and effector T cell function in tissues
LTB: Lymphotoxin-beta involved in inflammatory response and TNF-family signalling characteristic of activated effector memory cells
CD4 Effector Memory 69% dominant: 41.47-fold enrichment confirms this feature marks a distinct CD4 TEM metabolic state
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry sorting for CD4+CCR7-CD45RA- effector memory cells and measuring protein synthesis rates via SunTag labelling or puromycin incorporation, correlating with ribosomal protein expression.

programme_name: CD4 Treg with cytotoxic effector function
functional_description: This feature represents a specialized regulatory T cell programme combining immunosuppressive capacity with cytotoxic potential. The signature integrates IL-32-mediated inflammatory signalling, granzyme K cytotoxicity, and chemokine-mediated recruitment (CCL5/CCL4), alongside the checkpoint inhibitor TIGIT—consistent with suppressive Tregs that retain effector capabilities in inflammatory contexts.

GZMK: Granzyme K expression indicates cytotoxic potential, found in activated effector and suppressive regulatory T cells
TIGIT: Checkpoint receptor expression typical of activated/exhausted T cells and follicular helper Tregs regulating responses

functional_description: This programme represents metabolically active CD8 effector and central memory T cells with elevated oxidative phosphorylation capacity and enhanced chemokine secretion. The signature combines mitochondrial respiratory chain components with iron storage (FTH1) supporting sustained energy metabolism, alongside CCL5 production characteristic of memory T cell recruitment and antiviral function.
key_evidence: MT-CO3, MT-CO2, MT-ND1: Respiratory chain complex subunits indicating elevated OXPHOS capacity in memory T cells
FTH1: Iron storage gene supporting sustained mitochondrial function and metabolic demands of effector cells
CCL5: HIV-suppressive chemokine and memory T cell recruitment factor, hallmark of CD8 effector memory
CD69: Activation marker enriched in recently activated/tissue-resident T cells
Ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPS2, RPL4): Protein synthesis machinery supporting cytokine/chemokine production
suggested_validation: Sort top-activating cells by CD8+CD45RA-CCR7- phenotype and validate increased TMRM/MitoTracker intensity and CCL5 secretion by flow cytometry.

functional_description: This signature represents a metabolically active, proliferative state in CD4 central memory T cells during homeostatic maintenance rather than antigen-driven activation. The programme is dominated by biosynthetic machinery (ribosomes, tubulin, translation factors), iron metabolism (FTH1), and NAD+ synthesis (NAMPT), coupled with tonic TCR signalling restraint (RGS1, DUSP2/4) to maintain controlled proliferation in the bone marrow niche.
key_evidence: FTH1: Iron storage protein essential for rapidly proliferating cells managing oxidative stress during homeostatic turnover
RPS26, EIF3A, TUBB4B, TUBA4A: Translation and cytoskeletal machinery indicating active protein synthesis and cell division
NAMPT: NAD+ biosynthesis required for metabolic support of proliferating memory T cells in tissues
DUSP2, DUSP4, RGS1: MAPK/TCR signalling negative regulators preventing excessive proliferation despite tonic stimulation
HLA-DRB5: MHC-II expression consistent with CD4 T cell identity; enrichment in 34.5% CM subset
suggested_validation: Sort CD4 central memory T cells from bone marrow and validate elevated FTH1, NAMPT, and DUSP expression correlates with Ki-67+ cycling cells and reduced phospho-ERK upon TCR stimulation.

programme_name: Naive T cell ribosomal protein synthesis
functional_description: This feature captures a homeostatic translation programme characteristic of naive T cells (77% CD4/CD8 naive composition), marked by coordinated upregulation of ribosomal proteins and translation elongation factors. The dominance of ribosomal structural components (RPS2, RPS23, RPS17, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4) reflects elevated baseline protein synthesis capacity in quiescent naive T cells preparing for antigen encounter, rather than activation-induced synthesis.
key_evidence: RPS2/RPS23/RPS17/RPL37A/RPL7A/RPL4: Coordinated 40S and 60S ribosomal subunit proteins indicate active translation machinery assembly in naive compartment
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor supporting baseline protein synthesis in non-activated naive T cells
PTMA: Prothymosin-alpha involved in apoptosis resistance and cell proliferation, consistent with naive T cell homeostatic maintenance
NPM1: Nucleophosmin facilitates ribosomal protein chaperoning and nucleolus-cytoplasm shuttling during translation

programme_name: Activated memory T cells with metabolic stress
functional_description: This feature represents a metabolically active T cell programme enriched in effector memory and central memory CD8/CD4 T cells, characterized by high mitochondrial activity (MT-CO2, MT-CO3), actin dynamics (TMSB4X, ACTG1), and IL-32 expression suggesting recent or ongoing TCR stimulation. The elevated metabolic genes (LDHB, UCP2, ECH1) alongside ubiquitin (UBB) indicate active protein turnover and oxidative stress response typical of antigen-experienced cells.

TMSB4X & ACTG1: Actin regulators enriched in migratory/activated effector memory cells
MT-CO2 & MT-CO3: Mitochondrial OXPHOS subunits indicating high metabolic demand in effector cells
UBB: Elevated protein turnover and ubiquitin-dependent proteostasis in activated T cells
Cell composition: 16% CD8 EM2, 15.5% CD4 CM, 15.5% T proliferating; depleted in naive CD4/CD8
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry co-staining of IL-32, CD45RA/CCR7 (memory markers), and mitochondrial mass (TMRM) in sorted effector memory vs naive T cells.

programme_name: Activated memory T cells with enhanced protein synthesis
functional_description: This feature represents metabolically active, recently activated T cells with heightened translational capacity, predominantly CD4 central memory and naive cells. The signature combines immediate early response genes (JUN, FOSB) with ribosomal proteins and mitochondrial respiratory chain components, indicating cells undergoing active protein synthesis and ATP generation following TCR stimulation.
key_evidence: JUN, FOSB: AP-1 transcription factors mediating immediate early activation response to TCR/antigen engagement
RPL37A, RPS23, RPL7A, RPLP0, RPL4: Ribosomal proteins indicating elevated translation for effector molecule production

DUSP2: Negative feedback phosphatase on ERK/MAPK signaling, consistent with post-activation regulation phase
suggested_validation: Validate with flow cytometry assessing CD69+HLA-DR+ activation markers, intracellular staining for JUN/phospho-ERK, and MitoTracker staining to confirm elevated mitochondrial mass in the RPL37A+ ZFP36+ population.

programme_name: CD8 effector memory cytotoxic granule programme
functional_description: This feature represents terminally differentiated CD8 effector memory T cells with active cytotoxic granule biogenesis and secretion. The programme is dominated by serine proteases (granzymes A, B, H), cytotoxic effector molecules (perforin-associated), and chemokines (CCL4/5) that mediate target cell killing and immune cell recruitment. This reflects antigen-experienced cells primed for immediate cytolytic function against infected or transformed targets.

CCL4, CCL5: HIV-suppressive chemokines secreted by activated CD8+ effector cells for immune recruitment
CTSW: Cysteine protease upregulated by IL-2, essential for T-cell cytolytic mechanism
NKG7, GNLY: Granule-associated effector molecules constitutively expressed in activated cytotoxic lymphocytes

suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining for CD8, CCR7 (negative), CD45RA (negative), and GZMB/perforin positivity on sorted feature-high cells to confirm effector memory phenotype with active granule loading.

functional_description: This feature represents a metabolically active, proliferation-competent T cell state dominated by CD4 naive cells (42%) with elevated protein synthesis machinery and oxidative phosphorylation capacity. The signature reflects cells undergoing active translational activity and mitochondrial respiration, consistent with homeostatic proliferation or recent antigen-independent activation in the bone marrow niche.

functional_description: This feature represents a T cell state characterized by unusually high expression of hemoglobin subunit genes (HBD, HBM), ribosomal proteins (RPS26, RPS23, RPL37A, RPL7A), and immunoglobulin constant regions (IGKC, IGHA1, IGLC2). This signature is dominated by CD4 central and naive memory cells and likely reflects either contamination from erythroid/plasma cells, aberrant gene expression in activated T cells undergoing rapid protein synthesis, or a specialized plasma cell-like secretory programme.

programme_name: Activated effector memory with proliferative capacity

RPS26, RPS24, RPS2, RPLP0, RPL37A, RPL4: Ribosomal proteins indicating elevated protein synthesis for cytokine production and proliferation
TMSB4X, HSPA8: Actin sequestering and chaperone proteins supporting cell migration and protein folding during activation

functional_description: This feature represents actively proliferating T cells with elevated metabolic machinery, characterized by high expression of cytoskeletal proteins (TMSB4X, ACTG1), mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation enzymes (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, NDUFB9), and protein synthesis machinery (RPS24). suggested_validation: Sort bone marrow T cells by Ki-67 and EdU incorporation to confirm elevated mitochondrial gene expression (MT-COX, NDUFB9) and ribosomal proteins specifically in actively cycling cells.

programme_name: CD8 effector memory cytotoxic granule programme
functional_description: This feature represents activated CD8 effector memory T cells executing cytotoxic functions through granule exocytosis and chemokine-mediated immune recruitment. The signature is dominated by cytotoxic granule proteins (GZMA, CTSW, NKG7), chemokines with HIV-suppressive activity (CCL4, CCL5, CCL3), and signalling molecules supporting effector differentiation and TNF/IL-2 production.

CCL4/CCL5/CCL3: HIV-suppressive chemokines produced by activated CD8+ T cells for immune recruitment and antiviral responses
MAP3K8: Activates NF-κB and promotes TNF-α and IL-2 production during T cell effector activation

functional_description: This feature captures the active protein synthesis machinery characteristic of rapidly dividing T cells. functional_description: This feature represents a translational machinery and protein synthesis programme enriched in naive CD4+ and CD8+ T cells. The signature is dominated by ribosomal proteins (40S and 60S subunits), translation elongation factors, and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation components, reflecting high biosynthetic capacity during homeostatic proliferation or early G1 phase transition.

functional_description: This feature represents actively proliferating naive T cells engaged in homeostatically-driven cell division rather than antigen-driven activation. programme_name: CD8 effector memory cytotoxic granule programme
functional_description: This feature represents activated cytotoxic lymphocytes with a mature effector memory phenotype, characterized by robust expression of cytotoxic granule proteins (granzymes A/B/H, perforin) and chemokines (CCL4/5) that mediate target cell killing and immune recruitment. The dominant cell populations are NK cells and CD8 effector memory T cells, indicating a shared cytotoxic effector programme independent of recent antigen stimulation.

functional_description: This feature represents T cells undergoing active homeostatic proliferation and protein synthesis, characterized by elevated ribosomal proteins, translation initiation factors, and polyamine biosynthesis machinery. programme_name: Activated effector memory T cells with stress response
functional_description: This feature represents recently activated or stimulated effector memory T cells (predominantly CD4 and CD8 EM) undergoing rapid protein synthesis and metabolic reprogramming. functional_description: This feature represents actively proliferating T cells with elevated metabolic demand, characterized by enhanced mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and protein synthesis machinery. HMGN2: Chromatin remodeling factor maintaining open chromatin state required for active transcription during S/G2 phases

programme_name: Cytotoxic effector granule and protein synthesis
functional_description: This feature represents a cytotoxic T cell and NK cell programme characterized by active protein synthesis machinery combined with upregulation of cytotoxic granule proteins. NKG7: Natural killer cell granule protein, marker of cytotoxic effector programmes
RPS2, RPS24, RPL4, RPL7A, EEF1B2: Translation machinery components indicating high protein synthesis rate for effector molecules
CCND3: Cell cycle progression through G1/S, consistent with activated effector T/NK cell proliferation

functional_description: This feature represents a metabolic and housekeeping programme enriched in regulatory T cells (37% of top activators), characterized by iron metabolism, mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, and polyamine catabolism. SAT1: Polyamine catabolism regulates intracellular polyamine levels, linked to immune tolerance

UCP2: Mitochondrial uncoupling protein regulating ROS production and metabolic fitness in Tregs

programme_name: Naive T cell ribosomal protein synthesis
functional_description: This feature represents a homeostatic/proliferative programme in naive T cells characterized by high ribosomal protein and translation machinery expression. The signature is dominated by structural ribosomal components (RPS, RPL families) and translation elongation factors, indicating active protein synthesis capacity typical of dividing or metabolically active naive cells. The contamination of hemoglobin genes (HBA1, HBA2, HBB, HBD) suggests potential ambient RNA capture from bone marrow erythroid lineage rather than true T cell biology.

EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor supporting active protein synthesis during homeostatic proliferation

Cell composition: 50.5% CD4 naive + 27.5% CD8 naive (78% total) with 45.37x enrichment confirms naive T cell identity
suggested_validation: Validate with flow cytometry sorting of naive T cells (CD45RA+CCR7+) followed by bulk RNA-seq to confirm ribosomal protein enrichment independent of hemoglobin contamination, and assess whether this signature correlates with cell cycle activity (Ki67, PCNA) vs. resting state.

functional_description: This feature represents a metabolically active T cell state characterized by elevated ribosomal protein expression and enhanced translational capacity. FTH1: Iron storage protein upregulation reflects increased metabolic activity and oxidative capacity required for sustained protein synthesis
MT-CO2, MT-CO3: Mitochondrial respiratory chain components indicate elevated ATP production supporting anabolic processes
HNRNPA1: RNA-binding protein involved in pre-mRNA processing and mRNA metabolism, consistent with high transcriptional and translational flux
CD4 Central Memory (23.5%) and CD4 Naive (22.0%) dominant composition: Suggests homeostatic proliferation rather than antigen-driven exhaustion or terminal differentiation

functional_description: This feature represents actively proliferating T cells with elevated oxidative phosphorylation and protein synthesis machinery. The dominance of T Proliferating cells (41.5%) combined with enrichment of mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, NDUFB9) and ribosomal proteins (RPS24, RPLP0) indicates cells undergoing rapid division with high metabolic demand. RPS24, RPLP0: Ribosomal proteins signature of high protein synthesis rates required for cell division
TMSB4X: Actin-sequestering protein supporting rapid cytoskeletal reorganization during proliferation
IL32: T cell activation cytokine elevated upon mitogenic stimulation and TCR signaling
SLC25A3, SLC25A5: Mitochondrial transporter proteins supporting ATP/ADP exchange in energetically demanding dividing cells
suggested_validation: Confirm with Ki-67/PCNA co-staining and measure mitochondrial membrane potential (TMRM/JC-1) in purified T Proliferating cells versus quiescent T memory subsets.

programme_name: Naive T cell homeostatic protein synthesis
functional_description: This feature represents a basal biosynthetic programme dominated by ribosomal proteins and translation machinery, enriched in naive CD4+ and CD8+ T cells. The signature reflects active but non-antigen-driven protein synthesis characteristic of quiescent lymphocytes maintaining basal cellular functions, with concurrent oxidative phosphorylation support via mitochondrial genes.

RPL37A, RPLP0, RPL7A, RPL4: 60S ribosomal subunit components comprise complete ribosome assembly for homeostatic protein synthesis
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor essential for basal mRNA translation in resting T cells

functional_description: This feature represents activated cytotoxic T lymphocytes with granule-mediated killing capacity, characterized by expression of granulysin (GNLY) and cytotoxic machinery components. The signature is dominated by CD4 naive cells (36.5%) and CD8 effector memory cells (25%), suggesting a mixed population enriched for cytotoxic potential. TYROBP: ITAM-containing adaptor mediating activating signals in cytotoxic lymphocytes
FCER1G: Fc receptor gamma chain component of activating immune receptors
KLRD1: CD94 expressed on NK cells and cytotoxic T cells for NKG2-mediated activation
GPX1: Antioxidant protection during high metabolic demands of granule-mediated killing

AHSP + ALAS2: Erythroid-specific hemoglobin assembly and heme synthesis enzymes

19.52x fold-enrichment with hemoglobin dominance: Signature inconsistent with any T cell biology programme
