programme_name: Naive T cell ribosomal protein synthesis
functional_description: This feature captures a proliferation-associated translational machinery programme enriched in naive CD8 and CD4 T cells in bone marrow. The dominant expression of ribosomal proteins (RPS/RPL genes), translation elongation factors, and hemoglobin genes reflects active protein synthesis capacity, likely supporting rapid cell division and metabolic demands of recently activated or homeostatic-cycling naive populations.
key_evidence: RPS26, RPS23, RPS17, RPS24: 40S ribosomal subunit components indicating active translation initiation machinery
RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4, RPLP0: 60S ribosomal subunit assembly required for sustained protein synthesis during proliferation
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor supporting ribosomal peptide chain extension
HBA1, HBA2, HBB, HBD: Hemoglobin chain expression suggestive of high metabolic activity or potential iron handling in proliferating cells
48% CD8 Naive + 27.5% CD4 Naive composition with 12.21x enrichment indicates strong association with naive T cell homeostatic proliferation
suggested_validation: Use protein synthesis reporters (puromycin incorporation or BONCAT) and Ki-67 staining to confirm that this feature marks actively dividing naive T cells with high translational flux in bone marrow.

programme_name: CD8 effector memory cytotoxic granule programme
functional_description: This feature represents activated CD8 effector memory T cells with a dominant cytotoxic programme characterized by abundant expression of granzymes (GZMA, GZMH), granulysin (GNLY), and the cytotoxic granule protein NKG7. The co-enrichment of ribosomal proteins and CCL5 indicates these cells are actively synthesizing cytotoxic effector molecules while simultaneously producing chemokines to recruit additional immune cells.
key_evidence: GZMA, GZMH, GNLY: Core serine proteases and antimicrobial proteins packaged in cytotoxic granules, hallmarks of effector memory differentiation
NKG7: Natural killer granule protein 7, plasma membrane component essential for granule exocytosis and target cell killing
CCL5: Chemokine produced by activated CD8 effector cells; major HIV-suppressive factor and memory T cell recruiter
Ribosomal proteins (RPL/RPS): Elevated translation capacity required for high-rate synthesis of granzymes and other effector molecules
CST7: Cystatin F cysteine protease inhibitor; immune regulation protein consistent with activated cytotoxic T cell phenotype
suggested_validation: Sort CD8+ effector memory cells and validate via flow cytometry for CD45RA-, CCR7-, perforin+, granzyme B+ phenotype; confirm high granzyme protein content by intracellular staining.

programme_name: Regulatory T cell cytotoxic effector state
functional_description: This feature represents activated regulatory T cells (Tregs) co-expressing cytotoxic machinery and TCR signaling components, indicating a suppressive effector phenotype. The enrichment of LAT (TCR signaling), NKG7 (cytotoxic granules), and CST7 (immune regulation) alongside metabolic/cytoskeletal proteins reflects Tregs engaged in active suppression of effector responses.
key_evidence: LAT: Essential TCR adapter protein required for Treg activation and suppressive function initiation
NKG7: Cytotoxic granule protein enriched in activated Tregs with enhanced suppressive capacity via granule-mediated killing
CST7: Cysteine protease inhibitor with documented role in immune regulation, particularly in Treg populations
TMSB4X & ACTG1: Actin-regulating proteins supporting Treg migration and immune synapse formation during suppression
UCP2: Metabolic regulator involved in Treg lineage stability and suppressive function maintenance
suggested_validation: Sort feature-high CD4+FOXP3+ cells and confirm enrichment of NKG7+CST7+ Treg subset with functional suppression assays and TCR-stimulation dependence.

programme_name: Proliferating T cells with regulatory phenotype
functional_description: This feature represents actively proliferating T cells enriched in CD4 regulatory T cells and a subset of proliferating T cells. The signature is dominated by cytoskeletal dynamics (TMSB4X, ACTG1, COTL1), mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, NDUFB9), and nucleosomal remodeling genes (HMGN2, H3F3A) characteristic of rapidly dividing cells with high metabolic demand. IL32 expression suggests TCR activation signaling in this proliferative compartment.
key_evidence: TMSB4X, ACTG1, COTL1: Actin dynamics and cytoskeletal reorganization essential for cytokinesis and cell division
MT-CO2, MT-CO3, NDUFB9: Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation reflecting high ATP demand of proliferating cells
HMGN2, H3F3A, DEK: Open chromatin and active transcription marks typical of cell cycle progression
IL32: T cell activation cytokine induced by TCR signaling and mitogen stimulation
RPS24, HNRNPA1: Ribosomal and mRNA processing machinery supporting rapid protein synthesis during proliferation
suggested_validation: Sort cells by TMSB4X/ACTG1 expression and validate CD4+FOXP3+Ki67+ Treg and CD4+Ki67+ proliferating populations by flow cytometry with measurement of mitochondrial membrane potential to confirm metabolic activation.

programme_name: Homeostatic proliferation and translational stress response
functional_description: This feature represents a CD4-dominant naive and central memory T cell programme characterized by active protein synthesis machinery, iron metabolism, and polyamine biosynthesis—hallmarks of homeostatic rather than antigen-driven proliferation. The enrichment of ribosomal proteins, translation factors, and stress response chaperones suggests cells undergoing steady-state proliferation with concurrent metabolic stress management in the bone marrow niche.
key_evidence: RPS4Y1, RPS2, GSPT1: Ribosomal proteins and translation machinery indicate active translational activity and protein synthesis
ODC1: Rate-limiting polyamine biosynthesis enzyme essential for homeostatic cell proliferation without acute activation
FTH1: Iron storage protein reflecting elevated metabolic demands of proliferating cells in bone marrow microenvironment
HSPA9, PTMA: Heat shock proteins and apoptosis inhibitors indicating metabolic stress response during homeostatic cycling
SOCS3, GPR183, ZFP36: Cytokine response regulators and mRNA stability factors consistent with tonic signaling rather than acute inflammation
suggested_validation: Validate by ATAC-seq or ChIP-seq for markers of cell-cycle quiescence (CDKN1A) and compare ODC1/polyamine pathway activity to canonical activation markers (IL2, IFNG, TNF) to confirm homeostatic rather than inflammatory proliferation.

programme_name: Naive T cell oxidative metabolism priming
functional_description: This feature represents a transitional metabolic state in naive CD8 and CD4 T cells characterized by upregulation of oxidative phosphorylation machinery (mitochondrial electron transport complexes I and IV) combined with active protein synthesis capacity. This metabolic signature suggests priming for rapid proliferation and activation, potentially representing naive T cells preparing to enter or early in the activation phase within bone marrow niches.
key_evidence: MT-CO3, MT-CO2, MT-ND1, MT-ND5: Coordinated upregulation of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation complexes I and IV indicates elevated ATP production capacity characteristic of metabolically activated naive T cells
CD8B: 13th-ranked gene confirms dominance of CD8 naive cells (45.5%) in top activators, establishing CD8-enriched signature
RPS23, RPL37A, RPL7A, RPL4, RPS17: Multiple ribosomal proteins indicate concurrent protein synthesis machinery activation required for rapid clonal expansion
NPM1: Nucleophosmin involvement in ribosomal biogenesis and cell proliferation supports active growth phase consistent with activated naive T cells
AIF1: Calcium-binding protein induced by cytokines and interferons bridges metabolic activation with early immune signaling in proliferating T lymphocytes
suggested_validation: Validate by flow cytometry measuring OXPHOS activity (MitoTracker intensity), Ki-67 co-expression, and TCR stimulation kinetics in sorted CD8 naive vs memory populations to confirm this represents early activation metabolic priming rather than homeostatic maintenance.

programme_name: Proliferative T cells with active protein synthesis
functional_description: This feature represents actively proliferating T cells characterized by high expression of cytoskeletal proteins, chromatin remodelers, and metabolic machinery required for rapid cell division. The signature is dominated by genes supporting cell cycle progression, actin dynamics, and elevated protein synthesis capacity, consistent with homeostatic or antigen-driven proliferation in the bone marrow.
key_evidence: TMSB4X: Actin-sequestering protein essential for cell proliferation and cytoskeletal remodeling during active division
HMGN2: Nucleosomal binding protein associated with transcriptionally active chromatin maintaining open configuration for proliferation genes
STMN1: Microtubule destabilizer critical for mitotic spindle dynamics and cell cycle progression
CALM3: Calmodulin required for cell cycle regulation and cytokinesis completion
IL32: Cytokine induced by T cell activation; enrichment indicates activation-linked proliferation state

programme_name: Homeostatic proliferation central memory T cells
functional_description: This feature represents a proliferative programme in central memory T cells characterized by elevated expression of core metabolic and nucleotide biosynthesis machinery, alongside actin-cytoskeletal reorganization genes. The signature is dominated by housekeeping and proliferation-supporting genes (TMSB4X, STMN1, FTH1) with minimal inflammatory signals, suggesting antigen-independent homeostatic proliferation rather than activated effector differentiation.
key_evidence: TMSB4X: Actin sequestering protein essential for cell proliferation and migration, abundant in proliferating cells
STMN1: Microtubule destabilization factor controlling mitotic progression and cell cycle dynamics
FTH1: Iron storage and oxidative stress management, supporting metabolic demands of dividing cells
PTMA, HMGN2, HMGB1: Chromatin remodeling and transcription factors enabling accessible chromatin for proliferation genes
IL32: Cytokine expressed upon T cell activation but at baseline levels here, indicating homeostatic rather than inflammatory proliferation
suggested_validation: Sort CD4 central memory vs naive T cells and compare proliferation rate and Ki-67 expression to confirm this signature marks actively cycling memory cells in steady-state bone marrow.

functional_description: This feature represents a T cell sub-programme characterized by elevated ribosomal protein expression and translation machinery components, suggesting active protein synthesis capacity. The dominance of CD4 naive and central memory cells indicates this programme is associated with metabolically active, proliferative T cells preparing for or engaged in clonal expansion. The presence of hemoglobin genes and erythroid markers suggests possible contamination with bone marrow erythroid progenitors or indicates T cells with high metabolic activity characteristic of activated naive/memory populations.
key_evidence: RPS26, RPS23, RPS17, RPL37A, RPL7A: Multiple 40S and 60S ribosomal protein subunits indicate elevated ribosome biogenesis and translation capacity
RPLP0, EEF1B2: Translation elongation factors and ribosomal stalk components supporting active protein synthesis
NPM1: Nucleophosmin involved in ribosomal protein chaperoning and cell proliferation regulation
HBD, HBM, AHSP, CA1: Erythroid/hemoglobin markers suggesting either bone marrow context signature or metabolically intense T cells
CD4 Naive (34%) and CD4 Central Memory (21.5%) dominance: Consistent with proliferative lymphocytes requiring high protein synthesis capacity
suggested_validation: Validate by co-expression analysis with proliferation markers (MKI67, PCNA) and metabolic profiling (seahorse analysis of protein synthesis capacity) in sorted CD4 naive and central memory T cells versus quiescent effector memory T cells.

programme_name: CD8 effector memory cytotoxic granule programme
functional_description: This feature represents the cytotoxic effector programme of CD8+ effector memory T cells, characterized by abundant expression of cytolytic granule proteins (granzymes A/H, granulysin, NKG7) and chemokines (CCL5) for target cell lysis and immune recruitment. The co-expression of mitochondrial genes reflects the high metabolic demand of cytotoxic effector cells maintaining active killing machinery. This signature is consistent with antigen-experienced CD8+ T cells positioned for immediate cytotoxic function in tissue or secondary lymphoid organs.

NKG7: Granule membrane protein required for cytotoxic lymphocyte effector function
CCL5: Chemokine produced by activated CD8+ cells for immune cell recruitment and HIV suppression
CD8A: Definitive CD8+ T cell marker; co-expression with granzymes confirms cytotoxic lineage
MT-ND1, MT-CO2, MT-CO3: Elevated mitochondrial respiratory chain genes supporting ATP-intensive cytotoxic function

functional_description: This feature represents a quiescent or slowly proliferating regulatory T cell programme characterized by metabolic homeostasis and cytoskeletal dynamics. programme_name: Homeostatic proliferation with elevated metabolic activity
functional_description: This signature represents actively proliferating T cells with high oxidative phosphorylation capacity, dominated by CD4 naive and central memory cells. functional_description: This feature represents a metabolically active, proliferative T cell state characterized by elevated ribosomal protein expression and oxidative phosphorylation capacity. ATP5IF1, ATP5MC3, ATP5F1A, ATP5MC1, NDUFAF8: ATP synthase and oxidative phosphorylation components reflecting heightened metabolic demand for proliferation

functional_description: This feature represents actively proliferating T cells engaged in rapid protein synthesis and cell division, characterized by high expression of ribosomal proteins, RNA-binding proteins, and polyamine metabolism enzymes. ODC1, SAT1: Polyamine biosynthesis and catabolism enzymes supporting rapid DNA synthesis and cell division
PTMA: Anti-apoptotic factor and transcription regulator protecting proliferating cells from death
FTH1, TMSB4X: Iron storage and cytoskeletal remodeling supporting metabolic demands of proliferation

functional_description: This feature represents activated γδ T cells with innate-like cytotoxic and signaling properties, characterized by TCR δ constant chain expression, NK-like killer cell receptor engagement (KLRC1, KLRF1, KLRB1), and ITAM-based signaling (TYROBP, FCER1G). programme_name: Homeostatic proliferation and cell cycle activation
functional_description: This feature represents actively proliferating T cells with heightened metabolic and biosynthetic activity. The signature is dominated by genes involved in actin dynamics (TMSB4X, ACTG1), open chromatin remodeling (HMGN1, HMGN2), and core cell cycle machinery (STMN1, CALM3), indicating T cells engaged in rapid division rather than quiescence. The dominant enrichment in T Proliferating cells (70%) combined with elevated TRAC expression and IL-32 suggests recently activated T cells undergoing clonal expansion.

HMGN1, HMGN2: open chromatin remodeling factors enabling transcription of proliferation-associated genes
CALM3: calcium-dependent regulator of cell cycle progression and cytokinesis

TRAC + ribosomal/mitochondrial genes: active TCR expression coupled with elevated protein synthesis and oxidative metabolism (NDUFB9)

functional_description: This feature represents a proliferation-associated programme enriched in CD4 central memory and naive T cells, characterized by elevated ribosomal protein synthesis machinery, iron metabolism, and polyamine biosynthesis. The dominant gene signature reflects active protein translation capacity and cellular growth, consistent with homeostatic proliferation rather than antigen-driven activation.

FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain for iron storage, supporting metabolic demands of proliferating cells
ODC1: Ornithine decarboxylase catalyzes polyamine biosynthesis essential for cell division

GPR183: Chemokine receptor associated with lymphoid tissue homing and secondary lymphoid organ localization

functional_description: This feature represents actively proliferating CD4 effector memory T cells in a state of metabolic activation and cellular movement. functional_description: This feature represents actively proliferating T cells with elevated metabolic and cytoskeletal machinery, dominated by actin-binding proteins (TMSB4X, ACTG1, COTL1) and oxidative phosphorylation components. ACTG1: Cytoplasmic actin isoform essential for cytoskeletal dynamics during cytokinesis
MT-CO2/MT-CO3: Elevated mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation supporting ATP demands of rapidly dividing cells

HMGN2: Open chromatin maintenance gene supporting transcriptionally active state during cell cycle progression

programme_name: Early TCR activation with proliferative signaling
functional_description: This programme represents recently activated T cells undergoing early TCR-driven activation with active AP-1 transcription factor signaling and proliferative machinery engagement. The dominant cell types are CD4 central memory and CD8 effector memory cells, suggesting re-activation of previously primed T cells responding to antigen encounter in the bone marrow microenvironment.

CD69: Activation marker induced within minutes of T cell receptor engagement, hallmark of acute activation
ZFP36: Post-transcriptional regulation of inflammatory cytokine mRNAs (TNF, IL-2) via AU-rich element binding

TRAC: TCR constant region expression confirming active T cell receptor-mediated signaling events
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining for CD69+JUN+FOSB+ cells with phospho-ERK1/2 and phospho-p38 to confirm MAP kinase pathway activation downstream of TCR engagement.

functional_description: This feature represents a metabolic and translational activation programme dominated by CD4 and CD8 central memory T cells in the bone marrow. The signature reflects active protein synthesis, polyamine metabolism for cell division, iron storage management, and stress response machinery characteristic of proliferating memory T cells establishing or maintaining long-lived populations in the marrow niche.
key_evidence: ODC1, SAT1: Polyamine biosynthesis pathway (putrescine/spermidine synthesis and catabolism) indicating active cell cycle progression
FTH1: Iron storage protein suggesting metabolic stress management during proliferation in confined bone marrow microenvironment
LDHA, HSPA5, HSPA9: Glycolytic and mitochondrial stress response enzymes supporting energy demands of dividing memory cells
RPS4Y1, DDX21, SRSF3: Ribosomal and RNA processing machinery indicating high translational capacity
SOCS3, ZFP36, PDCD4: Post-transcriptional regulators of cytokine signalling suggesting homeostatic rather than acute activation
suggested_validation: Compare this signature with sorted CD4/CD8 central memory T cells versus naive T cells from bone marrow using metabolic flux analysis and immunophenotyping for Ki67 and phospho-STAT5 to confirm homeostatic proliferation without acute cytokine-driven activation.

functional_description: This feature represents activated cytotoxic lymphocytes (primarily CD8 effector memory T cells and NK cells) engaged in acute cytotoxic responses. The signature is dominated by granule-mediated killing machinery including granzymes, granulysin, and cathepsin W, coupled with stress response and inflammatory signaling pathways.
key_evidence: GZMB, GNLY, CTSW: Core cytotoxic granule proteins mediating target cell apoptosis via serine protease and cysteine protease pathways
NKG7, CST7: NK cell-associated granule proteins and cysteine protease inhibitors supporting cytotoxic function
FGFBP2: Selectively secreted by cytotoxic lymphocytes, enriched in effector memory populations
MAP3K8: Kinase activating TNF-alpha and IL-2 production during T lymphocyte activation and NF-kappaB signaling
CCL5, ZFP36: Chemokine and post-transcriptional regulator enabling recruitment and temporal control of inflammatory responses
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of CD8+CCR7-CD45RA- cells with GZMB+, perforin+, and CCL5+ markers, or functional cytotoxicity assays on sorted feature-high cells.

functional_description: This feature represents a translational machinery programme active in CD4 naive T cells during quiescent homeostatic states. The overwhelming enrichment of ribosomal proteins (RPS2, RPL37A, RPS23, RPS17, RPLP0, RPL4, RPL7A, RPS24) and translation elongation factors (EEF1B2) indicates active but constitutive protein synthesis required for basal T cell maintenance rather than activation-induced proliferation. The presence of SOCS3 suggests counter-regulatory signalling to maintain quiescence despite some cytokine exposure.
key_evidence: RPS2, RPL37A, RPS23, RPS17, RPLP0, RPL4, RPL7A, RPS24: Consensus 40S/60S ribosomal subunit components indicating robust translation machinery activity
EEF1B2: Translation elongation factor supporting ongoing protein synthesis capacity
FTH1: Ferritin heavy chain for iron homeostasis, marker of metabolically active but non-inflammatory cells
PTMA: Prothymosin-alpha involved in anti-apoptotic signalling and cell survival during quiescence
SOCS3: JAK/STAT inhibitor suggesting active suppression of cytokine-driven proliferation in naive compartment
suggested_validation: Sort CD4 naive T cells by surface markers (CCR7+CD45RA+) and compare ribosomal protein/translation factor expression to activated CD4 central memory cells; confirm SOCS3 expression inversely correlates with phospho-STAT3 in naive populations.

programme_name: Early TCR activation and metabolic engagement
functional_description: This feature captures the immediate post-TCR engagement phase, characterized by rapid induction of AP-1 transcription factors (JUN), early activation markers (CD69), and metabolic reprogramming for proliferation. The signature reflects concurrent ribosomal biogenesis, polyamine synthesis (ODC1), iron storage (FTH1), and stress-responsive pathways, indicating T cells transitioning from resting to activated states with active protein synthesis capacity.
key_evidence: CD69: Canonical early activation marker induced within minutes of TCR signaling across all T cell subsets
JUN: AP-1 component central to early TCR-driven transcriptional reprogramming and IL-2 production
ODC1: Rate-limiting polyamine biosynthesis enzyme essential for clonal expansion and cell cycle progression
FTH1: Iron storage upregulation supporting metabolic stress management during rapid proliferation
RPS2/RPS4Y1/DDX21: Ribosomal proteins and RNA processing factors indicating active translation machinery scaling
suggested_validation: Sort CD69+ versus CD69− T cells from bone marrow and validate enrichment of polyamine synthesis genes (ODC1, SAT1) and metabolic markers in CD69+ population; confirm this signature precedes acquisition of memory (CCR7, S1PR1) or exhaustion markers.

programme_name: Central memory T cell stress response
functional_description: This feature represents a stress-responsive programme enriched in CD4 and CD8 central memory T cells, characterized by simultaneous activation of cellular stress responses (heat shock proteins, DNA damage responses) and metabolic remodeling (iron storage, polyamine catabolism). The co-expression of CD69 with stress-response genes suggests cells responding to environmental perturbation while maintaining memory phenotype.
key_evidence: HSPA5 & HSPA9: ER and mitochondrial stress response chaperones indicating endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response activation
CD69: Early activation marker exclusively present in top-expressing cells, indicating recent or ongoing TCR engagement in memory cells
GADD45B & DDIT4: DNA damage and growth arrest response genes activated in response to cellular stress or nutrient limitation
FTH1 & SAT1: Iron storage and polyamine catabolism genes indicating metabolic remodeling and antioxidant stress management
ZFP36 & DUSP2: mRNA stability and MAPK pathway dampening genes suggesting post-activation phase with signal attenuation
suggested_validation: Validate using flow cytometry to confirm CD69+CD45RA- central memory phenotype co-expressing HSP70 family proteins and assess correlation with recent TCR stimulation or bone marrow environmental stress.

programme_name: Proliferating T cells with high metabolic activity
functional_description: This feature represents actively proliferating T cells with elevated oxidative phosphorylation and protein synthesis capacity. The dominant enrichment of T Proliferating cells (52%) combined with strong mitochondrial respiratory chain gene expression (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1, NDUFB9, UQCRQ) and ribosomal protein upregulation reflects the bioenergetic and anabolic demands of rapid cell division. The 37.39-fold enrichment suggests this is a highly specialized metabolic programme supporting clonal expansion.
key_evidence: MT-CO2, MT-CO3, MT-ND1: Five mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation genes in top-10 indicates high ATP demand for proliferation
RPS24, RPLP0, RPS2: Ribosomal proteins enriched for sustained protein synthesis during rapid cell division
TMSB4X: Actin-regulating protein required for cytokinesis and cell migration during proliferation
PTMA: Prothymosin-alpha anti-apoptotic function supports survival of rapidly dividing cells
T Proliferating cell enrichment: 52% of top-200 activating cells are T Proliferating, far exceeding other populations
suggested_validation: Sort bone marrow T cells by Ki-67 and BrdU incorporation, then validate MT respiratory chain and ribosomal protein upregulation in actively cycling (Ki-67+) versus quiescent populations by qRT-PCR or flow cytometry.

programme_name: CD4 Regulatory T cell homeostatic maintenance
functional_description: This feature represents quiescent or slowly proliferating CD4 regulatory T cells characterized by basal metabolic activity and cytoskeletal dynamics rather than active immune responses. The dominant enrichment in CD4 Regulatory cells (68.5%) combined with elevated mitochondrial genes (MT-CO2/3, NDUFB9, UCP2) and housekeeping factors suggests cells maintaining immune tolerance while sustaining minimal baseline metabolic functions.
key_evidence: CD27: TNF-receptor superfamily member essential for long-term T cell maintenance and regulatory T cell stability in bone marrow niche
IL32: Cytokine induced by T cell activation but also expressed by regulatory cells; involved in inflammatory modulation and cell survival
TMSB4X & ACTG1: Actin-regulating proteins supporting cytoskeletal integrity during slow migration and positioning within bone marrow microenvironment
Mitochondrial genes (MT-CO2, MT-CO3, NDUFB9, UCP2): Elevated oxidative phosphorylation reflecting steady metabolic state of non-proliferating but viable regulatory T cells
ISG20: Interferon-stimulated gene suggesting basal antiviral surveillance or response to homeostatic cytokines in regulatory T cell compartment
suggested_validation: Validate by co-staining feature-high cells with FOXP3, CD25, and HELIOS to confirm regulatory T cell identity, combined with metabolic assays to distinguish quiescence from activation.

programme_name: Recent activation with iron metabolism engagement
functional_description: This programme represents T cells in early-to-intermediate activation state, characterized by CD69 expression and active transcriptional responses to TCR/cytokine signalling. The high enrichment of ribosomal proteins and translation machinery indicates protein synthesis scaling, while elevated FTH1 and iron metabolism genes suggest metabolic reprogramming to support proliferation and cytokine production.
key_evidence: CD69: Early activation marker expressed upon TCR engagement, dominant in CD4 naive/memory composition
FTH1 + SAT1: Iron storage and polyamine metabolism upregulation supporting clonal expansion
RGS1 + DUSP2: Negative regulators of GPCR and MAPK signalling, limiting sustained activation signals
Ribosomal proteins (RPS4Y1, RPL37A, RPS17, RPS23): Protein synthesis capacity elevation during activation
ZFP36: AU-rich element binding protein regulating cytokine mRNA stability (IFN-γ, TNF stabilization)
suggested_validation: Flow cytometry co-staining of CD69 with iron staining (Prussian blue) and phospho-MAPK levels, combined with intracellular cytokine staining (IFN-γ, TNF) to confirm activation kinetics and metabolic state.

functional_description: This feature represents CD4 naive T cells with elevated ribosomal protein and translation elongation factor expression, indicating active protein synthesis machinery. The dominant representation of CD4 naive cells (60.5%) with secondary CD4 central memory cells suggests homeostatic proliferation or early activation state rather than terminal effector differentiation.
key_evidence: RPS26, RPS23, RPS17, RPS24: 40S ribosomal subunit proteins; coordinate upregulation indicates active translation initiation
RPL37A, RPL4, RPL7A, RPLP0: 60S ribosomal subunit proteins; suggest synchronized ribosome assembly and protein synthesis
EEF1B2: eukaryotic translation elongation factor; necessary for active protein synthesis elongation
HBA1, HBA2, HBB, HBD, HBM: hemoglobin chain expression; unexpected but may reflect erythroid contamination or bone marrow microenvironment-specific metabolism
S100A9: antimicrobial protein; minor signal suggesting early innate-like activation in CD4 naive population
suggested_validation: Confirm elevated protein synthesis rates by puromycin incorporation assays or phospho-ribosomal S6 staining in CD4 naive cells, and investigate whether hemoglobin expression reflects genuine T cell transcription or sorting/sequencing artifact from bone marrow niche interaction.

programme_name: Cytotoxic effector memory T cell activation
functional_description: This feature represents activated effector memory T cells with strong cytotoxic granule machinery and chemokine production. The signature is dominated by cytolytic proteins (perforin, granzymes A/B, granulysin, cathepsin W) and HIV-suppressive chemokines (CCL4, CCL5), characteristic of antigen-experienced CD8+ T cells mounting potent cytotoxic responses. While NK cells contribute significantly to the feature (46%), the T cell component (54%) is predominantly CD8 effector memory cells with established killing capacity.
key_evidence: PRF1, GZMA, GZMB, GNLY, CTSW: Complete cytotoxic granule arsenal indicating mature effector memory phenotype with active lytic machinery
CCL4, CCL5, CCL4L2: HIV-suppressive chemokines classically produced by activated CD8+ effector memory T cells
NKG7, KLRD1, KLRF1: NK cell markers explaining 39% NK component, but feature enriched in CD8 EM (14%) and EM2 (9.5%) populations
353.57x fold-enrichment: Exceptional specificity for cytotoxic lymphocyte populations versus broader T/NK compartment
CST7, TYROBP: Cysteine protease inhibitor and signaling adapter supporting sustained cytotoxic function
suggested_validation: FACS sort CCR7- CD45RA- CD8+ T cells and validate co-expression of perforin/granzyme B with CCL4/CCL5 production by flow cytometry or RT-qPCR to confirm effector memory identity.
